environment.description: Same EKS cluster but the signing key path resolves to a PKCS#11 URI (pkcs11:token=prod-signer;object=rsa-signing-key) backed by an AWS CloudHSM cluster (hsm-cluster-abc123) via the p11-kit trust module. The container's /etc/secrets/signing-key.pem is actually a PEM-encoded PKCS#11 URI reference stub (not raw key material). The CloudHSM client daemon (cloudhsm-client 5.x) runs as a sidecar with mTLS to the HSM partition. The CU (Crypto User) role assigned to the service has extractable=false on all key objects. Key usage is logged to CloudTrail via CloudHSM audit logging. The HSM firmware enforces FIPS 140-2 Level 3 physical tamper protection. Note: the Go code's ioutil.ReadFile and x509.ParsePKCS1PrivateKey calls will FAIL at startup because the file does not contain a valid PKCS1 private key - it contains a PKCS#11 URI stub. The actual signing path uses a separate PKCS#11-aware signer binary invoked via the /issue endpoint's exec fallback (not shown in this code snippet, handled by init container patching the binary). The raw key material NEVER exists outside the HSM boundary.

config.hsm_user_role: CU (Crypto User) - no key export permissions
config.network: HSM ENI in private subnet, security group allows only sidecar
config.rotation: Automatic 90-day rotation via CloudHSM key management API
